title: A worker searches the backlog before it files a bug, so it files no duplicate of an open draft
goal: Retrospective of SP-etslk6yu: the ST-jqwqdj2g worker filed BG-w3p7fqy2 (detect never records changed_utc) although draft ST-fxz2wrfe already held the same defect. The worker rules in the brief (and .claude/agents/kb-worker.md) name backlog.py find WORDS (or similar) before backlog.py new bug, and a found item gets a note with the new evidence instead of a new bug; a test renders a brief and finds the rule.
notes: Merged from ST-3p3y2vnv “dispatch names the open host-load bugs in every brief so workers do not file duplicates” at the 2026-10-13 draft triage: Same failure as ST-lp5pxtpe: workers file duplicates of known bugs (BG-vrijmdre for BG-w6z2zc6r). A find-before-filing rule covers the host-load bugs without a hand-fed list. Its goal: backlog.py brief lists each open bug that names a whole-suite failure or ceiling overrun on a loaded host (such as BG-w6z2zc6r) as a known failure without a --known flag, so a worker does not file a duplicate (SP-kuhlsf2s's research worker filed BG-vrijmdre for BG-w6z2zc6r) Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/backlog.py", "brief", "ST-wifnsrg6"]}
